source_user: Advanced cluster case multi-node NCCL-121: A multi-node NCCL job hangs only at larger world sizes. Produce a falsifiable diagnosis and rollback plan. Variant 121 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: test rank mapping, interface selection, topology, NIC affinity, rendezvous, firewall and ports, timeout logs, communicator formation, reduced-world baselines, and network counters. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Treat the hang as an observation, not proof of cause. Assumptions: the collective, message shapes, placement, launcher, software versions, and failing world sizes are reproducible; platform-specific facts must be measured. Record exact NCCL/CUDA/driver/framework/container/launcher versions, node and GPU inventory, rank-to-device and TP/PP/EP mapping, topology, selected interface and NIC/NUMA affinity, MTU/routes, InfiniBand/RoCE mode, rendezvous endpoint, authorized firewall/port policy, timeout settings, and synchronized clocks. Redact endpoints, tokens, and credentials.

Falsifiable hypothesis for variant 121: a scale-triggered rank, transport, or worker failure is hidden by the collective timeout. Hold workload, versions, placement, message sizes, and timeout policy constant. Binary-search the minimum failing world size and repeat each condition at least three times. Compare a known-good reduced-world run, the first failing world size, and a matched full-world run; change one factor per trial. Collect synchronized per-rank logs showing the last completed collective, rank/world size, elapsed time in seconds, communicator-formation result, selected transport/interface, and timeout. Correlate NCCL traces with switch/NIC counters in packets/s, bytes/s, retransmits, errors, drops, and link/queue utilization; capture topology and route evidence. Check rank mapping, interface selection, NIC affinity, rendezvous reachability, firewall and authorized ports, communicator formation, reduced-world baselines, and network counters before attributing cause. A hypothesis is supported only if the predicted rank/path symptom repeats and disappears under one controlled change without regressions.

Rollback: do not alter the production job first. Quiesce the canary, restore the last known-good NCCL/configuration and placement, drain or cordon only through the scheduler, and verify communicator formation plus a representative workload. Stop and restore immediately if any authorized canary exceeds the baseline timeout, shows new NIC/fabric errors, violates an SLO, or leaves orphaned processes. Report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, repetitions, and raw evidence; absence of evidence is not proof of improvement.
risks: Platform-specific behavior may differ from the stated assumptions.
A controlled canary or failure injection can affect shared capacity if not isolated.
Counters and logs may be incomplete or unsynchronized.
evidence_required: Matched baseline and repeated trial metrics with units

source_user: Advanced cluster case cluster scheduling and recovery-1: Design a resilient cluster scheduler for distributed LLM training and inference. Variant 1 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: cover gang scheduling, GPU/NIC/topology-aware placement, fragmentation, preemption, checkpoint cadence, node drain, elastic restart, replica routing, SLOs, and resource accounting. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Treat node failure as an observed event, not proof that scheduling alone is causal. Assumptions: the scheduler, workload, checkpoint format, routing layer, GPU/NIC topology, and node-health signals are measurable; exact platform behavior must be verified. Define resource units explicitly: GPUs, GiB, CPU cores, GiB/s network capacity, jobs/s, seconds, and dollars per GPU-hour where relevant. Record topology, workload mix, placement constraints, baseline queue time, utilization, fragmentation, restart time, checkpoint interval, recovery loss, throughput, error rate, and SLOs.

Falsifiable hypothesis for variant 1: topology-aware gang admission plus checkpoint-aware recovery reduces failed-job recovery time without increasing queueing or SLO violations. Compare the current policy with one controlled policy change on matched workloads and time windows, repeated across at least three comparable trials. The design must enforce gang scheduling for coupled DP/TP jobs, GPU/NIC/topology-aware placement, fragmentation accounting, priority and bounded preemption, checkpoint cadence, node drain, elastic restart only when the framework supports it, replica routing for inference, SLO-aware admission, and per-tenant resource accounting. Emit auditable events for allocation, preemption, drain, checkpoint, restart, routing, and reclamation; distinguish measured outcomes from estimates and control for workload, node mix, failures, and queue depth.

Failure and rollback: isolate unhealthy nodes, stop new placement there, preserve job/checkpoint metadata, and restart from the last validated checkpoint with bounded retry and duplicate-work protection. For inference, remove unhealthy replicas and route only to ready replicas; never route to a partially restored model. Roll back the policy or disable elasticity if p95 queue time, restart time, checkpoint loss, GPU/NIC placement violations, error rate, or SLO miss rate exceeds the predeclared baseline threshold, or if accounting/audit events are missing. Use least privilege, avoid exposing credentials, and verify recovery, resource reclamation, routing health, and no orphaned allocations before claiming improvement. Evidence required includes scheduler traces, topology and health snapshots, checkpoint manifests, per-job timings, utilization/fragmentation, SLO histograms, failure injections or naturally occurring failures, and matched-control analysis.
